--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[CPU-1] Sequential scheduled fetches block and can time out
File: src/inngest/functions/fetch-daily-closing-prices.ts (L1-L500)
Evidence: The Inngest job iterates symbols serially and awaits each symbol's batches and their network + DB upserts (for-loop with await per symbol and per batch). This makes total job duration grow linearly with symbol count and batch count, risking Inngest/serverless timeouts and huge execution queues.  
Impact: At 10x symbols or longer date ranges the job will exceed execution time limits or queue up many concurrent runs, causing missed schedules and provider throttling.  
Fix: Parallelize work by dispatching one job per symbol (or limited concurrency worker pool), or enqueue per-symbol tasks instead of awaiting all work inline.

[CPU-2] Per-record prisma.upsert in tight loops overloads DB
File: src/inngest/functions/fetch-closing-prices.ts (L1-L400)
Evidence: Both fetchAndStoreBatch/fetchAndStoreSymbol iterate records and perform await prisma.dailyClose.upsert(...) inside the loop (one DB call per record). This issues many small synchronous DB calls instead of batching.  
Impact: At 10x records this generates high DB connections/transactions and large latency, causing DB CPU saturation, long job times, and backpressure on the job runner.  
Fix: Batch writes (createMany with skipDuplicates, bulk upsert patterns, or grouped transaction) or buffer records and write in chunks rather than one upsert per record.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[CPU-3] Edge upload accepts 10MB files synchronously
File: src/app/api/diary/images/upload/route.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: The route reads multipart FormData and receives the full File object (maxSize 10MB) then uploads via @vercel/blob from within the request handler, keeping payload in runtime memory.  
Impact: If many concurrent uploads occur, edge/server runtimes can exhaust memory/connection limits and slow other requests (serverless concurrency limits hit).  
Fix: Offload uploads with client-side direct/presigned uploads to blob storage, validate Content-Length before body parse, or proxy streaming upload to avoid buffering entire file in the function.

[CPU-4] Client-side bulk CSV parsing is single-threaded and memory heavy
File: src/components/bulk-import-dialog.tsx (L1-L400)
Evidence: The component reads entire CSV via FileReader.readAsText, splits into lines, builds arrays/maps, sorts rows and resolves symbols all on the main thread (no worker/chunking).  
Impact: Large CSVs (10x rows) will hang or OOM the browser and make imports unusable for power users.  
Fix: Move parsing/resolution into a Web Worker or stream/chunk-parse the file and/or do server-side import with background processing.

--- INFO ---

[CPU-5] Unbounded single-retry recursion on rate-limited API
File: lib/closing-price-fetch-utils.ts (L1-L300)
Evidence: fetchFromGrowwAPI retries on 429 by awaiting sleep then calling itself again with no explicit retry limit.
